entities.name: Feidlimid mac Óengusa
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Feidlimid mac Óengusa, also known as Feidlimid Dub ('the Black'), ruled as King of Munster during the pivotal transition from late Roman Classical antiquity into the early medieval period of Ireland, approximately between 489 CE and his death in 501 CE. As a scion of the powerful Eóganachta dynasty, his reign consolidated the nascent political and religious shifts initiated by his father, Óengus mac Nad Froích, the first Christian king of Munster. His significance lies in his role in cementing the Eóganachta's dominance over southern Ireland and facilitating the integration of Christian customs into the traditional Gaelic kingship, thereby shaping the socio-political landscape of early historic Ireland.

Succeeding his father, Óengus, who according to tradition was baptized by Saint Patrick himself, Feidlimid inherited a kingdom undergoing profound transformation. While specific details of his reign are scarce in contemporary annals, he is credited with maintaining the Eóganachta's hegemonic influence over lesser kingdoms in Munster, including the Déisi and the Uí Liatháin. His tenure was characterized by the ongoing process of Christianization, which saw the establishment of early monastic sites and the gradual shift away from purely pagan practices in the royal court and among the wider populace. This period laid the groundwork for the flourishing of Irish monastic culture in subsequent centuries.
